mood.label: Bullish
mood.headline: Large caps look set to hold gains led by IT and Reliance, but weak smallcaps call for caution.
mood.summary: Nifty broke above its 22,757–22,844 resistance zone to about 22,933 (+1.37%) by 11 AM, and Sensex rose 1,062 points to 73,844, shrugging off a heavy Asian sell-off (Kospi −6.7%, Nikkei −4.7%). Cheaper crude (Brent $104.3, −1.7%) and a stronger rupee (94.86) set the tone, while IT extended its three-day run to about 8% ahead of Wipro and Tech Mahindra results tonight. The move is narrow: smallcaps are down 0.7–1%, PSU banks fell 1% on Canara Bank's 7% drop, and FIIs have sold for 14 straight sessions. If Nifty holds above 22,844 into the close, the breakout stands; a slip back below it would turn the day neutral again.

The rally is narrow: smallcaps are down 0.7–1% and PSU banks fall 1% as Canara Bank drops 7% and IDBI Bank 6%.

Wipro, Tech Mahindra (bonus), Nestle, Jio Financial and Polycab report after hours today; HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank report Saturday, and markets shut 20 Oct.

news.headline: Sensex jumps 1,062 points, Nifty tops 22,900 on IT and Reliance buying
news.summary: Sensex was at 73,844.10 (+1.46%) and Nifty 50 at 22,932.80 (+1.37%) at 11 AM, after a flat-to-firm open near 22,700. Cheaper crude and confidence in IT earnings drove buying despite a heavy sell-off across Asia.
news.why: Nifty has broken through its 22,757–22,844 resistance; holding above 22,844 by the close would confirm the breakout ahead of Saturday's big bank results.

news.headline: IT stocks rally for a third day; Tech Mahindra, HCL Tech, TCS up ~3%
news.summary: Nifty IT rose over 2% to about 30,806, taking its three-day gain to about 8.3%. Tech Mahindra (+3.4%), HCL Tech (+3.1%), TCS (+2.8%) and Infosys (+2.6%) led, ignoring the Nasdaq's 1.9% fall, as HCL Tech's strong results lifted hopes for the sector.
news.why: IT is carrying the index; Wipro and Tech Mahindra results after market hours today decide whether the run continues or fades on Friday.

news.headline: Smallcaps slide even as Sensex rallies; MTAR, HFCL, Netweb, Sterlite down ~5%
news.summary: Nifty Smallcap 100 fell more than 1% at one stage while large caps rose. IDBI Bank, HFCL, MTAR Technologies, Netweb, MRPL and CPCL were among the smallcap losers.
news.why: Narrow, large-cap-only rallies are fragile; for short trades in small stocks, the risk of a falling tide is higher than the index suggests.

news.headline: Canara Bank tumbles 7% as operating profit barely grows
news.summary: Q2 operating profit rose only to ₹8,758 cr from ₹8,588 cr a year ago as treasury income fell, overshadowing the 8.4% rise in net profit. The fall dragged the PSU bank index down about 1%.
news.why: Shows the market is judging banks on core earnings and treasury hits as bond yields rise; a warning sign before Saturday's private bank results.

news.headline: IDBI Bank falls 6% a day after Cabinet clears Fairfax sale
news.summary: After jumping 9% on Wednesday to about ₹90, IDBI Bank gave back 6% as traders booked profit. The deal price for Fairfax is ₹81 a share for 60.72%.
news.why: The stock still trades above the ₹81 deal price; open-offer terms are not out, so chasing it is risky.

news.headline: Tata Technologies jumps 8% despite weak quarterly profit
news.summary: The stock rose 8.32% to ₹807.55 even though Q2 profit missed estimates (the live blog cites a 5.2% fall from a year ago; other reports said +3% to ₹171 cr). Revenue grew about 28%.
news.why: The market is rewarding revenue growth and possible outlook comments over the profit miss; such reversals can fade if no follow-through buying comes.

news.headline: HDB Financial falls 4.7% after quarterly numbers
news.summary: HDB Financial Services dropped 4.7% to ₹556.30. Q2 profit rose 34% to ₹780 cr but came in below estimates.
news.why: Adds to pressure on NBFCs after Wednesday's sell-off in Bajaj Finance and Shriram Finance.

news.headline: CEAT slides 5% after results
news.summary: CEAT fell 5.1% to ₹3,186.70. Revenue rose 26% but profit was down sharply from a year ago (₹112 cr, −40%, per earlier reports).
news.why: Rubber and input costs are squeezing tyre margins; a negative read for peers like Apollo Tyres and JK Tyre.

news.headline: Leela Palaces hits record high after 27% profit rise
news.summary: Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts touched a fresh high of ₹649.80 on BSE after Q2 profit rose 27% to ₹94.6 cr.
news.why: Hotel demand is holding up into the wedding and holiday season.

news.headline: Rupee gains 31 paise to 94.86 on RBI steps and cheaper oil
news.summary: The rupee opened at 94.95 and touched 94.86 against the dollar, a fifth straight gain, helped by RBI's forex measures, a softer dollar (DXY 101.99) and Brent below $105.
news.why: A firmer rupee eases imported inflation and FII currency losses, but slightly trims the rupee price of gold ETFs.

news.headline: Brent falls about 1.7% to $104.3, off this week's $107 peak
news.summary: Brent traded near $104.30 (−1.66%) and WTI near $93.95. Reports that the US may ease 'shadow fleet' sanctions eased supply fears, though ship attacks near Hormuz continue.
news.why: Lower oil is the main reason for today's rally: it helps inflation, the rupee, oil marketers and paint makers, and hurts ONGC and Oil India.

news.headline: Asia sinks as AI trade cracks: Kospi −6.7%, Nikkei −4.7%
news.summary: South Korea's Kospi fell 6.74% to 5,603.77 and Japan's Nikkei 4.68% to 64,573; Taiwan fell 2.75%, Hang Seng 1.10% and Shanghai 1.62%. India bucked the trend.
news.why: Some see money rotating from expensive Asian tech toward India, but a deeper global sell-off would test today's rally.

news.headline: Reliance up 2.4% as Jio Platforms IPO lifts mood
news.summary: Reliance rose about 2.1–2.4%, supporting the indices. Jio Platforms' ₹30,213 cr IPO is priced at ₹1,065–1,119, with the anchor book on 19 Oct and subscription 21–23 Oct.
news.why: Reliance has fallen about 26% this year; the IPO could unlock value and has a shareholder quota.

news.headline: US inflation hotter at 3.7%; Nasdaq drops 1.88%, S&P 500 −1.11%
news.summary: September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% on the year, above the 3.6% forecast; core rose 2.6% vs 2.5%. Energy linked to the Iran war drove the headline. US IT stocks fell 3%, small caps 1.9%; the Dow held almost flat.
news.why: Revives Fed-hike bets for 28 Oct and hits tech valuations, a direct risk for Indian IT after its sharp run; also keeps FII money cautious.

news.headline: FIIs sell ₹1,857 cr for a 14th straight day; DIIs buy ₹2,670 cr
news.summary: Foreign investors stayed net sellers on Wednesday, slightly more than Tuesday's ₹1,305 cr. Domestic funds again absorbed the selling, as they have every day this month.
news.why: Steady domestic buying limits the fall, but the market struggles to rally while FIIs keep selling.

news.headline: Hormuz ship attacks hit a wartime high; Iran calls US offer 'insufficient'
news.summary: UKMTO logged 15 attacks on ships from 6 to 14 Oct, 11 in the last four days, and oil flows through the strait dropped sharply on 11 Oct. Iran says the US accepted some of its conditions but not all; no talks are scheduled.
news.why: Keeps a risk premium in oil; any further supply shock would hurt India's import bill, the rupee and inflation.

news.headline: Results today: Wipro, Tech Mahindra, Nestle, Jio Financial, Polycab, HDFC Life
news.summary: Tech Mahindra's board also considers a bonus issue (meeting 15–16 Oct). Persistent, L&T Finance, IIFL Finance and Angel One also report. Zetwerk, Tonbo Imaging and Sahajanand Medical IPOs open.
news.why: IT results will be judged against HCLTech's strong numbers and tonight's US tech mood; Nestle is the FMCG test.

news.headline: Gold rises about 1% after US CPI as the dollar slips
news.summary: Spot gold was at $4,143 (+0.89%) around 7 AM and near $4,167 (+1.4%) on another feed; silver gained 1.1%. The dollar index fell about 0.5% and US yields eased.
news.why: Supports Indian gold ETFs at the open, though the firmer rupee takes off part of the gain.

gold.label: Firm; rupee trims
gold.summary: Spot gold rose about 1% overnight to roughly $4,143–4,167 after hotter US inflation knocked the dollar (DXY 101.99, −0.54% this morning); no fresh midday MCX quote was found, so the last figure is ₹1,47,831 per 10g. The rupee's 31-paise gain to 94.86 trims about 0.3% off the rupee price, so gold ETFs like GOLDBEES are likely only modestly higher. MCX range to watch: ₹1,46,400–1,48,605; Fed-hike talk before 28 Oct is the main risk.
gold.how: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic gold rate: world gold in dollars × USD/INR, plus import duty. So both world events and the rupee move them.

scenarios.title: Dollar keeps sliding
scenarios.why: The dollar index fell about 0.5% to near 102 even after hot CPI, and gold rose about 1%. If that continues, world gold gains; a firmer rupee takes back a small part for Indian ETFs.
scenarios.when: DXY ~101.85–102.05 on 15 Oct; US PPI and retail sales data this week
scenarios.line: DXY −0.5% overnight lifted gold ~1%; the rupee trims part.

scenarios.title: Fed holds on 28 Oct (~68% odds)
scenarios.why: After hotter CPI, futures price about a 32% chance of an October hike (up from 22%), so a hold is still more likely. A clear pause would pull yields and the dollar down, which gold needs to get back above $4,225. The rupee may firm a little, trimming part of the gain in India.
scenarios.line: Yields and dollar ease; gold's best chance to get back above $4,225.

scenarios.title: Fed hikes on 28 Oct (~32% odds)
scenarios.why: Hot September CPI (3.7%) lifted hike odds to about 32%. A hike would push the dollar and US yields higher and could send gold back toward the $4,030–4,066 lows. FII selling in India would likely rise too, weakening the rupee and cushioning part of the fall.
scenarios.line: Odds up to ~32% after CPI; gold back toward $4,030–4,066.

scenarios.title: Gulf conflict widens, oil spikes
scenarios.why: Gold usually jumps on war fears, and higher oil weakens the rupee, so Indian gold ETFs gain on both counts. The catch: costly oil also feeds inflation and Fed-hike fears, which has capped gold's rallies recently, so gains can fade.
scenarios.when: Brent ~$104.7 (15 Oct); Hormuz ship attacks at a wartime high (15 from 6–14 Oct); Iran calls US response 'insufficient'
scenarios.line: Safe-haven buying plus a weaker rupee; can fade on inflation fears.

scenarios.title: US–Iran de-escalation
scenarios.why: Less war risk removes some safe-haven buying, though cheaper oil also lowers inflation and hike fears, which helps gold. The clearer effect for India is a stronger rupee, which pulls the rupee price of gold down.
scenarios.when: Iran says the US accepted some of its seven conditions but not all; no talks scheduled (Al Jazeera, 14 Oct)
scenarios.line: Less haven demand and a stronger rupee pull Indian gold down.

scenarios.title: Rupee slides past 97
scenarios.why: Every 1% fall in the rupee adds roughly 1% to Indian gold ETF prices even if world gold is flat. FII selling (14 straight days) and Brent above $100 are the pressures, but the rupee has gained four days in a row on RBI's steps.
scenarios.when: USD/INR vs 97 (record low 96.96); now 95.17 close; daily FII flows; Brent
scenarios.line: Each 1% rupee fall adds ~1% to gold ETFs, even with gold flat.

scenarios.title: Rupee recovers
scenarios.why: The rupee has gained 171 paise in four sessions (to 95.17) on RBI's dollar window for oil companies and curbs on speculation, a big reason MCX gold has lagged world gold. A further 2% recovery would knock about 2% off Indian gold ETFs.
scenarios.line: Rupee up 1.8% in 4 days; another 2% would cut ~2% off gold ETFs.

scenarios.title: Stock market sell-off
scenarios.why: Investors move money into gold when stocks fall. The WGC says weak Indian equities drove gold ETF buying in September. In a severe crash gold can dip briefly as people sell everything to raise cash, then recover.
scenarios.when: Nifty 22,622 vs 22,558 support; Kospi −5.6%, Nasdaq −1.9% overnight; VIX 14.62
scenarios.line: Money shifts to gold; September ETF buying was driven by weak equities.

scenarios.title: Central banks keep buying
scenarios.why: China's central bank added 21 tonnes in September, its 23rd straight monthly purchase. Steady official buying tends to limit how far gold falls, though it rarely drives short-term moves.
scenarios.line: China added 21 t in Sept (23rd month); limits downside.

scenarios.title: India cuts import duty
scenarios.why: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic price, which includes customs duty. A duty cut would lower the Indian gold price, and ETF prices, overnight by about the size of the cut, as happened in the July 2024 Budget. A duty hike would do the opposite.
scenarios.line: Domestic gold, and ETFs, drop overnight by about the cut.

guide._all: Each card is a company-specific event from the latest filings and news. Green = likely to support the share, red = likely to pressure it, amber = watch. Tap a type to see what usually happens next. New at midday: Leela Palaces' record high on a 27% profit rise (positive) and CEAT's 5% fall after results; Canara Bank turned negative after a 7% drop on weak operating profit, while Tata Technologies jumped 8% despite its miss. No client-loss or order-cancellation news found in filings up to midday. Review-by dates are counted in trading days (20 Oct is a market holiday).
guide.Can rise: Positive triggers. A share does not always rise on good news, especially if it ran up before the announcement or the overall market is weak.
guide.Can fall: Negative triggers. Results misses, big investor exits and weak business updates usually hit the share on the day and can weigh for weeks.
guide.Order won: An order matters most when it is big compared with the company's yearly revenue (5–10% or more is significant for smaller companies). Repeat orders and orders in a new area are good signs of future growth. Check the execution period: a 24-month order adds revenue slowly. Being named the only qualified bidder (Goodluck) is a step before an order, not an order itself.
guide.Results: Shares react to results versus expectations, not just growth. Profit growing slower than sales (DMart) signals squeezed margins, and the earnings call commentary often matters as much as the numbers.
guide.Business update: Monthly sales, pre-sales and festive data give an early read on the quarter before results come out.
guide.Board decision: Board outcomes that usually lift a share: buyback, bonus, stock split, special dividend, demerger or merger that simplifies the group. Ones that can pressure it: big equity fund raise (QIP or rights issue) that adds new shares, large acquisitions that need fresh capital (Aegis), or large related-party deals.
guide.Stake sale: When a promoter or big investor sells in a block deal, the share often falls on the day because the sale is at a discount. If quality institutions buy, it usually recovers within weeks.
guide.Regulatory: For pharma: a USFDA warning letter or import alert is a big negative, while a Form 483 with a few procedural observations (Dr Reddy's) is usually minor. Approvals, certifications and cuts in tax demands (Paytm) are positives; new or higher tax demands (Mphasis) and lawsuits (Bank of Baroda) are negatives, though most are disputed for years. Rule changes by NPCI, SEBI or the exchanges (UPI fees, F&O exits) can move a whole group of stocks.
guide.Management change: A sudden exit of a CEO or CFO can spook investors; a planned succession usually doesn't.
guide.Corporate action: Takeovers, open offers and delisting plans. These change who owns the company and can create short-term price moves. If the share already trades above the deal price (IDBI Bank), the upside depends on the open-offer terms.
guide.Fund raise: Debt or government loans don't dilute shareholders. Equity raises (QIP, rights, preferential issue) add new shares and can weigh on the price.
guide.Legal claim: A lawsuit or legal claim against a company. A big headline number can hit the share for days, but most claims take years and are often dismissed or settled for far less. Watch whether the court admits the case and what the company files.

items.title: Scrap LTCG tax on shares (and possibly cut STT)
items.who: Proposed by SBI Research · Decision: Finance Ministry
items.latest: SBI Research (12 Oct) proposed scrapping long-term capital gains tax on equities, with a 2–3 year holding period, to stem FPI outflows of ₹3.04 lakh cr this year. On 14 Oct the Finance Minister said it is 'too early to comment' and announced no change.
items.effect: If done, a big positive for the whole market and for FPI flows; brokers, exchanges and AMCs would gain most. Current LTCG is 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh. A cut in STT on F&O (raised to 0.05% on futures in April) would mainly help brokers and BSE.
items.likely: Low to medium: equity LTCG brought in about ₹1.29 lakh cr, hard to give up with a ~4.5% fiscal deficit
items.watch: Pre-Budget consultations (Nov–Jan) and any Finance Ministry comment

items.title: IDBI Bank sold to Fairfax (60.72% stake at ₹81/share)
items.latest: On 14 Oct the Cabinet approved Fairfax's ₹52,878 cr bid: the government sells 30.48% and LIC 30.24% at ₹81 a share. IDBI jumped 9% to ₹90.39 on 14 Oct, then fell about 6% by 11:30 AM on 15 Oct as traders booked profit. Government keeps 15%, LIC 19%.
items.effect: Largest privatisation since Air India and a boost to reform sentiment. For IDBI shareholders, the stock already trades above ₹81; open-offer terms for public shareholders are not yet announced, so chasing the jump is risky. Fairfax must merge or exit CSB Bank, where it owns 40%.
items.likely: High (approved); RBI fit-and-proper and CCI clearances still needed
items.watch: Open-offer price and size; RBI approval; government's plan to sell its remaining 15%

items.title: More PSU stake sales (OFS) this year
items.latest: About ₹55,757 cr raised so far in FY27 from stake sales in 9 PSUs (including LIC and Coal India). With IDBI, receipts cross the ₹80,000 cr target for the first time in 8 years. The government may sell its residual IDBI stake in the market.
items.effect: An offer-for-sale (OFS) is usually priced at a discount, so the PSU stock often dips for a few days around the sale. Meeting the target can reduce pressure for further big sales this year.
items.when: Through March 2027; OFS dates are announced a day ahead
items.watch: OFS announcements on NSE/BSE (usually the evening before)

items.title: RBI rate decision: another hike likely in December
items.latest: RBI hiked the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 Oct. September CPI came in at 5.54% (above the 5.4% forecast). HDFC Bank, DBS, Oxford Economics and others now expect 25 bps more in December; some see 50–75 bps more this year.
items.effect: A hike raises borrowing costs: negative for rate-sensitive stocks such as NBFCs, real estate and autos, and for bond prices. Banks can gain on margins at first. A pause would be a relief rally trigger.
items.likely: High for a 25 bps hike, based on economist forecasts

items.title: India–US trade deal
items.who: Commerce Ministry and US Trade Representative
items.latest: As of 14 Oct, talks are in the final stretch on a framework drafted in February 2026. Market access for Indian goods and US industry protections are still open issues; a final announcement is 'not immediate'.
items.effect: A deal that lowers US tariffs would help exporters that depend on the US: textiles and apparel, gems and jewellery, auto parts, chemicals, seafood. Failure or new tariffs would hit the same group.
items.when: Not fixed; possibly weeks to months

items.title: SEBI closing auction for the final price
items.latest: SEBI received 3,500+ comments on a Closing Auction Session to set closing prices more fairly; a circular is expected soon. Investor-awareness messages on broker apps start 1 Nov.
items.effect: Changes how the closing price is set at 3:30 PM. Mainly affects traders and index funds; little effect on long-term holders. Exchanges and brokers may need system changes.
items.when: Circular expected soon; start date to be announced

items.title: GST process reforms
items.latest: The GST Council approved process reforms at its 8 Oct meeting to speed decisions and cut compliance; the Prime Minister welcomed them. Details of each change are still being notified.
items.effect: Lower compliance cost helps small businesses and consumer companies over time; no immediate rate change.

items.title: US Federal Reserve rate decision
items.latest: Markets price about 80% odds of a hold on 28 Oct but a hike by December. The US 10-year yield is near 5.2%, close to a 24-year high.
items.effect: A hold is mildly positive for Indian stocks, the rupee and gold. A surprise hike would lift the dollar and US yields, push FIIs to sell more, and hurt IT and gold.

items.title: US midterm elections and Iran risk
items.latest: Midterms are on 3 Nov. President Trump said there will be no US strike on Iran before then; the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted.
items.effect: After 3 Nov the Iran pledge expires, so oil and safe-haven risk could rise. Higher oil hurts India (rupee, inflation, oil marketing companies, paints, airlines) and helps gold and upstream oil.

items.title: OPEC+ oil output for December
items.latest: On 4–5 Oct OPEC+ kept November output unchanged. The next monthly decision (for December) is due in early November.
items.effect: Higher output would ease crude and help India's rupee, inflation and oil marketing companies. A cut would do the opposite.

items.title: Union Budget 2027
items.latest: Preparations are under way. The LTCG/STT debate, disinvestment, capex and the fiscal deficit (~4.5% of GDP) will be the key themes.
items.effect: Tax changes on capital gains or STT, customs duty on gold, and capex plans can move whole sectors on the day.
items.watch: Pre-Budget meetings and leaks from December
